title: Three large developments and provincial housing law changes
subtitle: Courtland Avenue former Schneider site, Bleams Road subdivision, Highland Road tower, digital neighbourhood meetings and missing-middle housing pace
overview: The Planning and Strategic Initiatives Committee recommended that Council approve three development proposals. These were a Mattamy Homes subdivision at Bleams Road and Gehl Place, a large mixed-use community on the former Schneider's factory lands along Courtland Avenue East, and a high-rise rental building at Highland Road and Spadina Avenue. The Courtland proposal includes 135 affordable units, a public park and a contribution to a local affordable housing project. The Highland Road proposal drew objections from nearby residents about traffic, height and shadows.

The committee also recommended a package of city-initiated changes to respond to provincial Bills 13, 109 and 23. They let staff handle minor zoning amendments, update site plan and demolition control rules, revise public participation policy and add two planning staff positions. An attempt to make neighbourhood meetings hybrid rather than digital was defeated {{vote:m5}}.

Several councillors pressed for faster as-of-right triplexes and fourplexes. Staff said the work is limited by their current workload and can be considered later. These are committee recommendations and still need Council's adoption.

decisions.item: Bleams Road and Gehl Place subdivision
decisions.detail: The committee recommended draft plan approval, an Official Plan amendment and rezoning for the Mattamy Homes subdivision, which allows up to three units in street-fronting townhouses and semi-detached homes.

decisions.item: Courtland Avenue East former Schneider site
decisions.detail: The committee recommended draft plan approval, an Official Plan amendment, rezoning and adoption of the urban design report for a mixed-use community with a public park and 135 affordable units.

decisions.item: Highland Road and Spadina Avenue high-rise
decisions.detail: The committee recommended, as amended to adjust yard setbacks and a Highland Road step-back, adopting the Official Plan amendment, approving the rezoning and endorsing the urban design brief for 130 and 140 Highland Road and 270 Spadina Avenue.

The committee recommended Official Plan and zoning changes, delegating minor zoning amendments to the Director of Planning, updated site plan and demolition control by-laws, revised public participation policy, repeal of two affordable housing development charge policies, and two more planning staff.
The committee rejected a proposal to change digital neighbourhood meetings to hybrid meetings in the implementation report {{vote:m5}}.

debate: On Courtland Avenue, councillors asked about traffic from the site onto Borden Avenue and whether a roundabout could be used instead. Staff said the traffic study led to turn lanes, signals and a one-way exit only onto Borden, which they described as an improvement over the former truck traffic.

Some councillors asked whether the Courtland park could be moved closer to the street. Staff said the park grew during negotiations, sits beside the privately owned public space and connects to active transportation routes. Others asked whether more density could be added in return for deeper affordable housing, and staff said they would report back.

At Highland Road, residents opposed the tower over traffic on a two-lane road, shadows on homes, a lawn bowling club and a heritage district, and the scale of the building. One resident supported the project but asked for better transit and cycling. One councillor questioned the height, the zero-metre front setback and the location outside a major transit station area. Staff said the corner site allows a closer setback, and that the building steps back from nearby homes.

On neighbourhood meetings, one councillor argued digital-only meetings exclude residents without internet access. Staff said attendance has held steady, participants are more varied, callers can join by phone, and one-on-one or on-site meetings are offered when needed.

Several councillors wanted as-of-right triplexes and fourplexes sooner than the Official Plan review. Staff said wider changes need more resources and that the current approach is a measured first step. They also reported lost development charge revenue since Bill 23.
